turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a, an and the?
turns.tutor:
Sure! I'll start by solving an example so you can see my thinking.
She eats an apple. The word after the gap is "apple". It begins with a vowel sound, so I write an, not a.
The rule in one line: use an before a vowel sound and a before other sounds.
Right: I have a pen. Wrong: I have an pen.

Here is your exercise. Write only one word:
Write a or an: She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
turns.judgeInput:

C1 (correct) strength 1: a singular countable noun needs a/an (or the). Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
